1. Evidence and the 75-80% score requirement

Reviewed sample

All 150 objective prompts and 30 offered descriptive prompts in supplied 2021-2025 FM papers were reviewed. No FM section is listed in the supplied 2019 compilation; 2026 is Phase I only. Modern descriptive choices cannot be projected from older ESI data.

Both halves are necessary

Each 2021-2024 compilation offers three finance and three management descriptive prompts. The 2025 compilation offers four finance-oriented prompts, including AI/ethics overlap, and two management prompts. This is offered-question classification, not an official fixed finance/management mark split or permission to omit a half.

What repeats most dependably

Communication and motivation/personality/perception-related material occur in every modern FM paper when objectives and descriptives are considered together. Ethics/governance also spans all five. Finance repeatedly tests institution/regulator roles, instruments, payments, rules and policy applications. Exact forms change.

A realistic target equation

Using the recent 50+50 structure: objective 40 + descriptive 35 = 75; objective 43 + descriptive 37 = 80. These are planning combinations, not predicted achievable marks. At objective 35, even descriptive 40 only reaches 75.

Negative marking and source limits

Use correct-mark value - one-quarter wrong-mark value, not raw question accuracy when one-/two-mark items coexist. The 2025 source itself flags objective Q28-30 as possibly inexact in question/theme. Keep those as provisional examples, not exact wording evidence. Verify current rules against applicable RBI/SEBI releases.

Breadth rule

Cover every explicit finance and management heading in the supplied syllabus. Prepare core subjects deeply, but keep a minimum concept/application layer for accounting, derivatives, alternate finance and less frequent management models.

2. Financial system, institutions and regulation

What to study

Financial intermediation, RBI functions, banking structure and developments, NBFC/HFC differences, and SIDBI/EXIM/NABARD/NHB/NaBFID mandates. Know purpose, clients, funding/product and development role; distinguish regulator, operator and institution.

Objective versus descriptive depth

Objectives ask recognition, regulator and rule/application. A descriptive answer must explain channels: mobilisation -> intermediation -> credit/risk allocation -> development, with institutional distinctions. Evidence: 2021 objective Q6/Q14-16, DQ4; 2023 objective Q21; 2024 Q9-12; 2025 Q1-4 and DQ5.

Regulation and supervision

Distinguish prudential/conduct rules, supervision, systemic oversight and consumer protection. Learn capital, liquidity, leverage, asset-quality and governance concepts, including the logic of Basel pillars. Evidence: 2021 DQ5; 2024 objective Q30; 2025 DQ5. Do not memorise a Basel ratio without meaning and scope.

Global system and international banking

Prepare crisis contagion, liquidity/funding, FX/capital-flow risk, cross-border banking and the transmission of global shocks into India. Evidence: 2022 DQ5. Know broad trends and current regulatory responses, not every foreign bank detail.

Stop line

Skip detailed institution annual accounts, obscure circular clauses and deep international-banking legal mechanics. Retain major updated thresholds and exceptions when they are relevant to the syllabus/PYQ-style rules.

3. Markets, risk, derivatives and alternate finance

Market structure and instruments

Study primary/secondary, money/bond/equity/forex, participants, issuance, trading, clearing and settlement; T-bills, CP/CD, repo, government bonds and basic equity/mutual-fund concepts. Compare maturity, issuer, risk, return and use. Evidence: 2022 objective Q8-11; 2023 Q30; 2025 Q3-6.

What objective depth looks like

Recognise an instrument from a situation; apply a threshold/rule; identify the regulator/platform; distinguish debt from equity and settlement from issuance. ASBA (2021 Q7-8; 2024 Q5-8) and receivables discounting (2025 Q18-20) show the value of process maps rather than acronym lists.

Risk management

Credit, market, interest-rate, liquidity, operational, cyber, model and systemic risk: definition -> exposure -> consequence -> control -> residual risk. Distinguish capital from liquidity and asset-price from funding risk. Use Basel and banking examples, not advanced statistical risk-model derivations.

Derivatives

Compare forwards, futures, options and swaps; rights/obligations, exchange/OTC, margin/counterparty risk, hedger/speculator/arbitrageur. Work simple hedging/payoff direction cases. Evidence: 2024 DQ1 asks types, participants, significance AND risks. Do not replace this with just four definitions or study stochastic option pricing.

Bonds and investing

Explain price-yield direction, duration intuition, default/subordination/call risk and ordinary versus AT1 features. Compare value/growth investing by valuation, expected earnings and risk; avoid stock tips. Evidence: 2024 DQ5/Q6. Keep applicability and instrument-specific conditions clear.

Alternate finance and PPP

Cover venture/private capital, crowdfunding at a conceptual level, REITs/InvITs, infrastructure finance, PPP models and private versus social cost-benefit. Evidence: 2021 objective Q9-11; 2023 Q28; 2024 Q22; 2025 Q5-6. Explain risk allocation, externalities, incentives and viability, not just full forms.

A 75-80% depth check

Can you draw the transaction flow, distinguish two similar products, solve a simple numeric/application item and write benefits/risks/safeguards on an unseen instrument using the underlying concepts? If not, rereading the chapter is not sufficient.

4. Accounting, Budget and inflation: protect the breadth

Accounting coverage

Know accounting equation, asset/liability/equity, revenue/expense/profit, accrual versus cash, balance sheet/P&L/cash-flow links. Calculate and interpret debt-equity, debtor/creditor days, inventory turnover, ROA and ROE using the stated definitions/periods.

Exact observed forms

2021 objective Q26 compares valuation with otherwise similar bank information; 2023 Q22 calculates ROA; 2025 Q7-9 asks gross profit, debt and liabilities from data. Work small mixed problems and check units, numerator, denominator and averages. Do not dismiss accounting as too rare; do not expand into a professional-accountancy syllabus.

Budget and public finance

Revenue/capital receipts and spending, deficit measures, debt, grants/transfers, non-tax revenue, financing and the current Budget's broad priorities. Evidence: 2021 objective Q21 and DQ1; 2023 objective Q29; 2025 Q23 and DQ4. Be able to classify an item and explain its economic effect.

Inflation

CPI/WPI coverage and components, headline/core, demand-pull/cost-push, base effects, expectations, distributional costs and monetary/fiscal remedies. Explain why divergent CPI/WPI movements can occur. Evidence: 2025 objective Q17/Q24 and DQ4; Q28's inexact-source caveat applies. Skip advanced macro modelling.

Policy application

Explain transmission and lags, not 'raise rates to reduce inflation' alone. Distinguish supply shocks from excess demand and discuss growth/inflation trade-offs. Read relevant Budget/Survey/MPC summaries, not every tax schedule.

5. Digital finance, inclusion and governance

Digital/IT and inclusion

Understand payment-system roles and flows, bank/non-bank participants, CBDC/UPI/cards/account distinctions, digital lending, fintech, access/usage/quality and last-mile barriers. Examples: 2021 objective Q4-5/Q20; 2022 Q21; 2023 Q1-5 and DQ6; 2024 Q28; 2025 objective Q18-22.

Descriptive digital pattern

2022 DQ3 asks blockchain disruption; 2023 DQ3/Q4/Q6 asks Retail Direct, ONDC and credit-line UPI; 2025 DQ6 asks AI risks and ethics. Study purpose, mechanism, participants, benefits, limitations and safeguards. A product-launch note is not a complete descriptive answer.

AI depth without engineering overload

Cover bias/fairness, explainability, model validation, data privacy, cybersecurity, third-party concentration, accountability and human oversight. Link each risk to a use case and control. No need to derive machine-learning algorithms for these prompts.

Corporate governance in banking

Study board/committee roles, oversight versus execution, independence, conflicts, risk culture, audit, disclosure and stakeholder protection. Evidence: 2021 DQ3; 2023 objective Q11-15/Q20. Keep current composition rules separate from the underlying governance principles.

Mixed connections

A digital-lending case can test financial risk, consumer protection, ethics and governance simultaneously. A PPP case combines finance and incentives. A regulatory change can affect inclusion and operational risk. Prepare these links explicitly instead of maintaining isolated chapters.

6. Management: full syllabus, theory and application

Foundations and schools

Management functions and roles; scientific, administrative, human-relations and systems approaches; nudge theory. Compare unit of analysis, assumptions, application and limitation. Evidence: 2023 DQ1 (Fayol); 2025 objective Q12-14. Skip thinker biographies and memorised labels without scenarios.

OB, personality, reinforcement and perception

Individual/group/organisation levels, Big Five, determinants of personality, reinforcement versus punishment, attribution/perceptual errors. Evidence: 2021 Q1-3/Q22/Q24 and DQ6; 2022 Q1-3/Q26; 2023 Q23 and DQ2. Practise the same behaviour under plausible competing labels.

Motivation: all explicit theories

Maslow, ERG, McClelland and Herzberg (content); Adams equity and Vroom expectancy (process). Know central construct, assumptions, prediction, workplace example and limitation. Compare motivation/hygiene, equity/equality and expectancy/instrumentality/valence. Examples: 2022 Q15-17; 2023 Q7-8; 2024 Q21; 2025 Q27.

Leadership and emotional intelligence

Trait, behavioural, contingency, charismatic, transactional and transformational; EI concept, dimensions and organisational use. Identify the mechanism, context fit and limitation, not just the theorist. Evidence: 2021 DQ2; 2023 Q9-10; 2024 Q25 and DQ3. Use a comparison matrix plus a short case.

Relationships, conflict and change

Transactional analysis and Johari Window; conflict sources/types/management styles; resistance, Lewin, OD, action research and positive model. Evidence: Johari 2021 Q24/2024 Q24; change 2022 DQ2/2025 DQ2. Practise diagnosing causes before proposing interventions.

Minimum coverage for less-visible headings

EI, conflict, nudge, transactional analysis and OD alternatives remain in the official syllabus even if the sample underrepresents them. Prepare definition, dimensions, one scenario and one outline. Absence from five papers is not evidence of exclusion.

The theory card

Theory | core proposition | variables/stages | a workplace case | nearest confusable theory | limitation. Retrieve the card closed-book, then classify a new case and explain why its nearest alternative is weaker. This is deeper than recalling a mnemonic.

7. Ethics, governance and communication: applied depth

Ethics breadth

Utilitarianism, rights/duties, justice/fairness, care, virtue, teleological views, egoism and relativism. Apply to compliance, finance, HR and marketing. Cover organisational structure, board responsibilities, ethics programmes, code of ethics/conduct and governance mechanisms.

The observed pattern

2021 DQ3: governance need/principles; 2022 DQ6: managerial ethical behaviour; 2023 DQ5: implementing a code; 2024 DQ4: ethical influences; 2025 DQ6: financial AI ethics. A memorised ethics definition will not cover implementation.

A usable ethics-case method

Identify stakeholders, facts and conflict; compare duties/rights/outcomes/fairness; assess feasible alternatives; justify an action and safeguards. Include accountability, reporting/escalation and monitoring when relevant. Do not recite every theory regardless of fit.

Communication breadth

Process and feedback; channels/networks; oral/written and verbal/non-verbal; upward/downward/lateral; barriers and IT. Explain noise and remedy at sender, message, channel and receiver. Distinguish a network's structure from direction.

Communication examples

Objectives recur across all five years. Descriptive prompts include barriers/remedies (2022 Q1), channels/importance (2024 Q2), and non-verbal communication across leadership, culture and collaboration (2025 Q3). A single generic 'communication is important' answer will miss these different demands.

Change and ethics combined

For a new AI/banking workflow, diagnose fear, incentives, capability and trust; plan communication, training, participation and feedback; add fair oversight and evaluation. Use a named model only when it genuinely organises the answer.

8. How to study, practise and earn descriptive marks

Best source stack

Use one full-note source per topic from your Finance/Management folders. First solve a small diagnostic set, read the relevant concept, then use objective practice, answer-writing questions, short notes and infographics for different purposes. Use official RBI/SEBI material to update rules; notes' dates are not proof of currency.

Practice both knowledge modes

For management: retrieve theory -> classify scenario -> compare alternatives -> write application/limitations. For finance: draw flow -> compare instruments -> solve small numeric/rule cases -> write purpose/benefits/risks/safeguards.

Match the answer to the demand

For 2024 derivatives, cover types, participants, significance and risk. For a leadership comparison, use common dimensions and examples, not two disconnected mini-essays. For a named policy, give its actual mechanism before broad advantages.

Score calibration

Use the same 90-minute planning budget as ESI: selection, two 15-mark and two 10-mark answers, review. Under current-style instructions that is 50 descriptive marks, not six compulsory essays. Verify selection rules in the actual notice.

High-score safeguards

Do not drop accounting/derivatives; do not assume management alone covers all objective questions; do not quote obsolete regulatory values. Avoid long theory lists, repeated points, empty 'awareness' solutions and polished but irrelevant introductions.

Readiness

Keep net objective scores near your planning target on fresh 30-minute sets. Get timed descriptive work reviewed for demand coverage, conceptual correctness, application, evidence, balance and language. Reviewer marks are calibration only, not predicted RBI scores; assess repeated performance, not a single good paper.

Studying with mind maps, tables and worked examples

Management: theory comparison table

Columns: Theory | Core idea | Recognition clue | Application | Common confusion. Herzberg | Hygiene and motivators have different roles | Conditions versus achievement | Diagnose dissatisfaction separately | Removing dissatisfaction need not create motivation. Vroom | Expectancy, instrumentality, valence | Effort -> performance -> valued outcome | Check capability, reward credibility and value | A valuable reward alone is insufficient. Adams | Perceived input-outcome fairness | Comparison with another employee | Investigate perceived inequity | Equity is not identical rewards.

Test the table through a mini-case

Case: an employee values promotion but believes performance will not influence selection. Identify the relevant theory, explain the broken link and propose a remedy. Under Vroom, the performance-to-outcome link (instrumentality) is weak. Now change the case so the employee doubts their ability to perform: explain why the diagnosis changes. These are learning illustrations, not PYQ solutions.

Finance: draw the transaction

TReDS example: MSME supplies goods/services -> buyer accepts invoice -> financiers bid to discount the receivable -> MSME receives early payment -> buyer pays at maturity. Add: purpose, participant at each step, conditions, risks and safeguards. Use the same process-map method for payments, bond issuance, monetary transmission and PPPs.

Instrument comparison template

Columns: Instrument | Issuer/parties | Purpose | Return/payment | Main risks. Compare two confusable instruments on the same dimensions. Then cover the instrument name and identify it from the remaining fields.

Accounting practice table

Columns: Ratio | Formula/convention | Meaning | Small calculation | Interpretation trap. Always solve a numeric example and explain the result. Check the stated definition, period and use of average balances. Formula recognition is not calculation competence.

Combine methods for depth

Use a small topic map for structure, a table for distinctions, a flowchart for mechanism and a new case for application. For descriptive practice, select the relevant theory/mechanism, apply it and discuss limitations rather than copying the map.

Making visual notes stick: recall and practice

Match the tool to the knowledge

Mind map: topic structure. Flowchart: how something works. Comparison table: similar items. Fact table/cards: values, dates and exceptions. Mini-case: application. Question-specific outline: descriptive writing. Error log: recurring mistakes.

Blank-page recall: the essential step

Close the source. Rebuild the map/table from memory. Explain the connections aloud. Compare with the source and correct missing/wrong elements. Attempt a fresh question. Recognising a finished map is not the same as knowing the topic.

Spaced retrieval

A practical starting schedule is next day -> one week -> two weeks -> one month, adjusted to recall. Hide table columns, reverse the prompt, vary the case and retrieve the relationship as well as the label. Update dated facts before reinforcing them.

A manageable 60-minute session

20 minutes: understand from existing notes. 10: make one small map/comparison table. 10: reconstruct closed-book. 15: apply through MCQs, a case or an answer outline. 5: record mistakes and the next review. For English, replace part of reading/organising with actual writing. Adapt the timings; do not make formatting the main activity.

The stopping rule

Every visual note must produce recalled facts, solved questions, explained cases or a written answer. If formatting takes more effort than testing, simplify. The goal is retrievable knowledge, not an attractive notebook.

How to interpret this audit

These are paraphrased offered prompts, not model answers or proof that the same topic will return. Recent papers list three 15-mark and three 10-mark options; use the actual selection instructions. Objective evidence references above are separate from descriptive Q numbers. DQ means descriptive question.

A 12-week integrated preparation path

Weeks 1-2: diagnose and establish breadth

Take fresh objective ESI/FM diagnostics and write one full English paper. Map every syllabus heading green/amber/red by closed-book performance, not reading completed. Establish core economics, financial-system basics and management theory cards. Start writing immediately, not after finishing all notes.

Weeks 3-5: deepen and connect

Work through ESI scheme/report cases, FM instruments/accounting/risk and applied management. Write timed answers on multiple syllabus areas; practise precis and RC weekly. Add current developments to existing static notes instead of building a second unrelated notebook.

Weeks 6-8: objective-to-descriptive transfer

Use mixed objective sets and choose answers from six-question descriptive menus. Test both mark bands and complete all English tasks. Repair stale facts, confused rules, weak mechanisms and incomplete subparts. Keep one current-affairs source.

Weeks 9-10: full-paper constraints

Run fresh timed papers with a keyboard and actual-style selection rules. Review mark-weighted objective net scores and externally reviewed writing separately. Do not hide one subject's weakness behind the aggregate.

Weeks 11-12: revision and verified updates

Prioritise retrieval, comparison sheets, short error logs and repeated timed completion. Update major reports/policies from applicable official releases. Limit new sources and stop expanding low-return detail.

Weekly outputs and readiness gate

Once foundations are established, work toward one fresh timed objective section and one full descriptive section each for ESI and FM, plus one full English paper per week. Review and rewrite before adding volume. Seek repeated objective performance around 40-43/50 net and independently reviewed complete answers around your planning targets; do not turn an unofficial review into a score guarantee. Track each subject separately across at least three fresh papers.

Protect Phase I work

If Phase I is only two months away, this is a parallel Phase II track, not a direction to abandon Phase I aptitude/GA. Start with one feasible Phase II content block and one short writing/recall block daily; increase after Phase I. Adapt time to your baseline and available hours.

Using your material without drowning in it

Assign each resource one job

Full notes explain; objective questions test discrimination; descriptive questions test organisation/application; short notes support retrieval; infographics refresh a map. Do not read all five versions cover-to-cover or make another full notebook.

Reverse-learning loop

Fresh question -> classify the gap -> targeted full-note repair -> short closed-book explanation -> a new application question -> spaced retest. Distinguish knowledge missing, rule confusion, stale value, weak analysis, poor selection and time failure.

One compact topic packet

Keep a concept map; one comparison table; a few dated evidence anchors; objective exceptions/rules; two descriptive skeletons; and your error list. One or two pages is a revision goal, not a restriction that forces important syllabus detail to disappear. Detailed notes remain the reference.

Currency and verification

Your Reports_NationalAndInternational, SchemesAndGovernmentPortals and CurrentAffairs-Monthly folders are useful starting material. File names/editions are not certification of current accuracy. Check official scope, release/reference date and policy effective date before using numbers in an exam.

English resource gap

No dedicated English folder appears under SubjectNotesForPhase2. Use the supplied usable English tasks and fresh passages for production practice; ESI/FM notes supply content, not a substitute for writing/precis feedback.

Evidence limits and official source stack

Authority

The official supplied syllabus is a 2025 Phase II excerpt. Exam timings, marks and choice structure used for planning are corroborated by the supplied guidebook pp26-27 and paper labels, not a supplied complete 2027 notification. Confirm final structure and instructions from RBI before the exam.

What the sample cannot establish

No candidate scripts, examiner rubrics, actual awarded descriptive marks or question-level empirical solve times were supplied. Therefore this guide cannot rank topics by proven scoring ease, promise 75-80, or infer exact future marks. Five modern papers support patterns, not a narrow guaranteed list.

Use historical questions correctly

Learn the concept/fact template, not stale figures. The guide paraphrases demands rather than endorsing every recollected premise. Automated old topic tags were not used as verified frequency counts. Offered prompt counts are not distinct concepts, candidate attempts or mark shares.

Official updates

RBI: https://www.rbi.org.in/ ; SEBI: https://www.sebi.gov.in/ ; Budget/Survey: https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/ ; MoSPI: https://mospi.gov.in/ ; PIB: https://pib.gov.in/ . Use the relevant ministry/report issuer for scheme eligibility and report-specific findings.

How to use the companion HTML

The HTML has clickable source and notes-folder links plus the same full analysis. PDFs provide bookmarked printable copies. The CSV exposes all 60 ESI/FM descriptive prompts and the JSON preserves the English task audit.

English: 75-80% preparation

Want one specific topic to give an AI agent? English writing/comprehension tasks and prompts. Each topic states the exact concepts, calculations or exercises to cover, with linked chapter notes.

Original printable subject analysis PDF

The new detailed inventories and distribution are in this HTML; the linked original PDF does not include that extension. Use browser Print to PDF to save the complete updated report.

1. What the evidence says: a writing paper, not Phase I English

Sample and stable task mix

All five supplied 2021-2025 English sections offer essay, precis and written comprehension, labelled 40/30/30 marks. The 2019 section offers the same three skills as supplementary evidence. Each essay offers choices; they are not all attempted.

Word-limit change in the supplied sample

2021-2022 recollections specify about 300 essay words and 170 precis words; 2023-2025 specify about 600-620 essay words and 180-200 precis words. Use the actual exam instruction. Do not train exclusively on the old shorter format or impose a one-third precis rule when an explicit limit is given.

75-80% score route

A planning combination is essay 30/40 + precis 23/30 + RC 22/30 = 75; 32 + 24 + 24 = 80. These are goals, not a published scoring rubric or a promise. A strong essay cannot fully compensate for unfinished precis/RC.

Important source mismatch

2021 PDF pp71-72 prints an agorism passage but insurance-sector comprehension questions. Those subquestions cannot be reliably answered from that passage. Exclude this pair from evidence-based RC marking; do not invent missing material. The other 2021 tasks remain usable for practice.

The real depth requirement

Express a defensible argument; compress a text faithfully; explain relationships from an unfamiliar passage in your own words. Content familiarity helps speed, but reading fidelity, structure and language determine the quality of the response.

2. Essay breadth: prepare families, not predictions

Technology, business and work

Coding education, BPO, creativity (2021); e-rupee, employee motivation and multilingual business communication (2023); digital advertising and startup adaptation (2025). Prepare productivity, access, jobs/skills, competition, privacy, governance and ethics.

Climate, energy and development

Renewable energy and grid integration (2022); climate economics (2023); climate migration (2024); emissions-intensity commitments (2025). Prepare mechanisms, distributional effects, finance, trade-offs and practical implementation.

Social/human capital and organisations

Women entrepreneurs and medical tourism (2022); employee mental health and lifelong learning (2024); intergenerational education (2025). Prepare education, health, inclusion, gender, ageing and workplace capability.

Abstract and multidimensional prompts

Prevention versus cure (2021), peace through understanding (2022), lifelong learning (2024) show that pure economics preparation is insufficient. Olympics impacts (2024) requires social, economic AND environmental dimensions. Learn argument construction for unfamiliar subjects, not a model essay for every headline.

A compact evidence bank

For each family keep 3-4 mechanisms, 2 examples, 1 reliable fact when useful, 2 counterarguments and workable responses. Reuse ESI/FM knowledge selectively. An English essay is not a dump of report names or scheme abbreviations.

Stop line

Do not memorise full essays, ornamental quotations or hundreds of statistics. Do not predict the next topic from repetition. Keep breadth through varied prompts and fresh outlines, not more passive reading sources.

3. Essay depth: argument, structure and editing

Selection before commitment

Choose the topic on which you can state a thesis, cover every requested dimension, give concrete examples and acknowledge a meaningful limitation. A familiar word in a title is not sufficient. Spend a short fixed time deciding, then commit.

Plan a coherent line of argument

Define the issue and position in the opening; order body paragraphs causally or by the question's dimensions; include counterargument/conditions; conclude with a reasoned judgement. Each paragraph should advance the thesis, not merely add a heading.

Paragraph method

Claim -> explanation/mechanism -> evidence/example -> link to the question. For climate migration, distinguish origin and destination impacts; for a technology prompt, distinguish capability from implementation conditions. This prevents generic filler.

Word allocation

For a roughly 600-word essay, a starting plan is about 60-80 words introduction, 420-460 body and 60-80 conclusion. Adapt to the exact limit and topic. A word target is a constraint, not a reason to repeat an argument.

Language

Prefer accurate, direct sentences and controlled vocabulary. Vary sentence structure only when clear. Check subject-verb agreement, article/preposition use, pronoun reference, tense, parallelism and punctuation. Avoid unsupported absolutes and invented quotes/data.

Editing order

First check demand coverage and logic; then paragraph transitions and repetition; then language and word limit. Polishing adjectives before fixing a missing subpart is low-return work.

Practice target

Write varied timed essays, not just outlines. After review, rewrite the weakest paragraph and outline a different topic to test transfer. A reusable structure must still accommodate an unfamiliar prompt.

4. Precis: faithful compression is a separate skill

What recurs

The subjects vary: sand extraction (2021), space race (2022), AI/gender (2023), AI leadership (2024), Amazon climate risk (2025). The stable demand is to retain the central argument and relationships under a tight word limit.

A repeatable method

Read for thesis and structure; mark main propositions, causal links and qualifications; separate essential support from illustration; draft in your own words; count words; compare the draft against the source for omissions, distortion and additions.

Compress ideas, not random sentences

Generalise a list only when the common category is accurate. Remove repeated examples and narrative detail before dropping a main claim. Preserve contrast, cause/effect, degree of certainty and the author's stance. Reordering is acceptable only when the argument remains faithful.

Examples of dangerous distortion

Turning 'may increase risk' into 'will cause failure'; retaining only benefits from a balanced AI passage; dropping the distinction between suitable construction sand and abundant desert sand. These are comprehension errors, not stylistic preferences.

Title and expression

Provide a concise neutral title when instructed. Keep the summary self-contained, coherent and free of personal opinion, invented evidence or meta-commentary. Do not write a critique or a bullet-list substitute unless instructed.

Review checklist

Main thesis retained? All major stages covered? Key qualifications preserved? No outside facts/opinion? Natural prose? Accurate title? Within the stated limit? Use this for diagnosis; it is not an official mark conversion.

Best practice

Practise 180-200 words on the recent supplied tasks, plus varied fresh passages. Compare coverage maps before comparing vocabulary. Rewriting a bad summary faithfully is more valuable than collecting model precis answers.

5. Written comprehension: answer the question, not the topic

The repeated operations

Retrieve a reason; explain a process; compare alternatives; identify consequences; synthesise dispersed details; state the author's argument. Later papers offer five subquestions. Subject matter shifts, so practise unfamiliar technical/business prose.

Observed examples

2022 asks why commodity-market regulation was separate and effects of merger; 2023 asks inflation measurement and distribution between profits/workers; 2024 asks CRM functions, deployment comparisons and challenges; 2025 asks water needs, osmosis, advantages and future technology.

Evidence-map method

For each question underline the command and scope, locate all supporting spans, note required points, then paraphrase without changing the technical meaning. Check that every sentence answers the question. Do not copy a large paragraph.

Depth and length

Use the stated answer limit if present. Otherwise calibrate to marks and number of requested points; do not write an essay per subquestion. Multi-part questions need all parts, even if one is less familiar.

What not to do

No outside facts unless requested, no personal policy recommendation in a retrieval question, no answer from the topic title alone and no guessed mechanism. Technical terms can remain when paraphrasing them would distort meaning.

Time trap

Repeatedly rereading the whole passage instead of mapping a specific demand wastes time. Use local evidence for retrieval, but read wider for contrast or inference. Do not use the mismatched 2021 pair to judge your accuracy.

6. Training, timing and honest score calibration

A 90-minute starting plan

For current-style 40/30/30 tasks, try essay 35 minutes, precis 25, RC 25 and 5 minutes final checks. This includes reading/planning within each task; it is not an official optimal allocation. Practise another order if it improves completion without damaging essay/precis quality.

Typing is part of the task

Use a keyboard with no autocorrect/spellcheck during timed practice. If four FM/ESI answers were written to the supplied 600/400 maxima, that is about 2,000 words before planning/review. For a 600-word English essay in 35 minutes with 8 minutes planning/checking, about 22 clean words/minute of composition is needed. Measure thoughtful composition, not copied-text typing speed.

A weekly minimum to adapt to baseline

Two essays, two precis, two RC sets and one complete timed English paper is a useful training starting point; count full-paper tasks toward the totals. Review/rewrite sessions matter as much as volume. Reduce quantity if feedback and correction are being skipped.

Rubric for feedback - unofficial

Essay: relevance/demand, argument, organisation, support, language and completion. Precis: fidelity, coverage, compression, coherence and instruction compliance. RC: correct required points, textual support, paraphrase and concision. Ask reviewers to identify concrete missing/distorted points, not just award a number.

Readiness standard

Complete every task within instructions and time across several unseen papers. Seek independent review of at least two full scripts and compare reviewer disagreements. A self-awarded 80 is not evidence of an official 80. Track recurring error rates and task completion alongside indicative scores.

The largest avoidable losses

Unfinished RC; precis that adds opinions; off-topic essay; missing a dimension; incorrect data used for decoration; ignoring a changed word limit; and no time left for basic editing. Eliminate these before chasing sophisticated vocabulary.

Studying with mind maps, tables and worked examples

Essay: question-specific argument map

Centre: the exact question and requested dimensions. Branch 1: central position/thesis. Branch 2: argument -> explanation -> example. Branch 3: second argument -> explanation -> example. Branch 4: counterargument or limitation. Branch 5: judgement and way forward. Then write the essay. Outlines alone do not train sentences, transitions or completion.

Precis: passage-structure table

Columns: Paragraph | Main proposition | Relationship | Essential? Example row 1: introduces the problem | Context | Retain briefly. Example row 2: explains why it happens | Cause | Retain. Example row 3: several illustrations | Examples | Compress. Example row 4: limits the claim | Qualification | Preserve. Draft from the main propositions, then check against the original. Do not change certainty, causation or the author's stance.

Comprehension: evidence table

Columns: Question asks | Relevant passage points | Answer in my words. Map every part of the demand to textual evidence, then write a concise response. The table is a practice scaffold, not something to reproduce in the examination.

Personal language-error table

Columns: My error | Correct form | Why | My new sentence. Record errors you actually make, then write a fresh sentence applying the correction. This is more useful than repeatedly collecting grammar rules already mastered.

Do not confuse organising with writing

Mind maps help planning, but English improves through reading accurately, producing prose, receiving feedback and editing. Replace part of note-making time with a timed paragraph, precis or comprehension answer. Review ideas before vocabulary.

Making visual notes stick: recall and practice

Match the tool to the knowledge

Mind map: topic structure. Flowchart: how something works. Comparison table: similar items. Fact table/cards: values, dates and exceptions. Mini-case: application. Question-specific outline: descriptive writing. Error log: recurring mistakes.

Blank-page recall: the essential step

Close the source. Rebuild the map/table from memory. Explain the connections aloud. Compare with the source and correct missing/wrong elements. Attempt a fresh question. Recognising a finished map is not the same as knowing the topic.

Spaced retrieval

A practical starting schedule is next day -> one week -> two weeks -> one month, adjusted to recall. Hide table columns, reverse the prompt, vary the case and retrieve the relationship as well as the label. Update dated facts before reinforcing them.

A manageable 60-minute session

20 minutes: understand from existing notes. 10: make one small map/comparison table. 10: reconstruct closed-book. 15: apply through MCQs, a case or an answer outline. 5: record mistakes and the next review. For English, replace part of reading/organising with actual writing. Adapt the timings; do not make formatting the main activity.

The stopping rule

Every visual note must produce recalled facts, solved questions, explained cases or a written answer. If formatting takes more effort than testing, simplify. The goal is retrievable knowledge, not an attractive notebook.

A 12-week integrated preparation path

Weeks 1-2: diagnose and establish breadth

Take fresh objective ESI/FM diagnostics and write one full English paper. Map every syllabus heading green/amber/red by closed-book performance, not reading completed. Establish core economics, financial-system basics and management theory cards. Start writing immediately, not after finishing all notes.

Weeks 3-5: deepen and connect

Work through ESI scheme/report cases, FM instruments/accounting/risk and applied management. Write timed answers on multiple syllabus areas; practise precis and RC weekly. Add current developments to existing static notes instead of building a second unrelated notebook.

Weeks 6-8: objective-to-descriptive transfer

Use mixed objective sets and choose answers from six-question descriptive menus. Test both mark bands and complete all English tasks. Repair stale facts, confused rules, weak mechanisms and incomplete subparts. Keep one current-affairs source.

Weeks 9-10: full-paper constraints

Run fresh timed papers with a keyboard and actual-style selection rules. Review mark-weighted objective net scores and externally reviewed writing separately. Do not hide one subject's weakness behind the aggregate.

Weeks 11-12: revision and verified updates

Prioritise retrieval, comparison sheets, short error logs and repeated timed completion. Update major reports/policies from applicable official releases. Limit new sources and stop expanding low-return detail.

Weekly outputs and readiness gate

Once foundations are established, work toward one fresh timed objective section and one full descriptive section each for ESI and FM, plus one full English paper per week. Review and rewrite before adding volume. Seek repeated objective performance around 40-43/50 net and independently reviewed complete answers around your planning targets; do not turn an unofficial review into a score guarantee. Track each subject separately across at least three fresh papers.

Protect Phase I work

If Phase I is only two months away, this is a parallel Phase II track, not a direction to abandon Phase I aptitude/GA. Start with one feasible Phase II content block and one short writing/recall block daily; increase after Phase I. Adapt time to your baseline and available hours.

Using your material without drowning in it

Assign each resource one job

Full notes explain; objective questions test discrimination; descriptive questions test organisation/application; short notes support retrieval; infographics refresh a map. Do not read all five versions cover-to-cover or make another full notebook.

Reverse-learning loop

Fresh question -> classify the gap -> targeted full-note repair -> short closed-book explanation -> a new application question -> spaced retest. Distinguish knowledge missing, rule confusion, stale value, weak analysis, poor selection and time failure.

One compact topic packet

Keep a concept map; one comparison table; a few dated evidence anchors; objective exceptions/rules; two descriptive skeletons; and your error list. One or two pages is a revision goal, not a restriction that forces important syllabus detail to disappear. Detailed notes remain the reference.

Currency and verification

Your Reports_NationalAndInternational, SchemesAndGovernmentPortals and CurrentAffairs-Monthly folders are useful starting material. File names/editions are not certification of current accuracy. Check official scope, release/reference date and policy effective date before using numbers in an exam.

English resource gap

No dedicated English folder appears under SubjectNotesForPhase2. Use the supplied usable English tasks and fresh passages for production practice; ESI/FM notes supply content, not a substitute for writing/precis feedback.

Evidence limits and official source stack

Authority

The official supplied syllabus is a 2025 Phase II excerpt. Exam timings, marks and choice structure used for planning are corroborated by the supplied guidebook pp26-27 and paper labels, not a supplied complete 2027 notification. Confirm final structure and instructions from RBI before the exam.

What the sample cannot establish

No candidate scripts, examiner rubrics, actual awarded descriptive marks or question-level empirical solve times were supplied. Therefore this guide cannot rank topics by proven scoring ease, promise 75-80, or infer exact future marks. Five modern papers support patterns, not a narrow guaranteed list.

Use historical questions correctly

Learn the concept/fact template, not stale figures. The guide paraphrases demands rather than endorsing every recollected premise. Automated old topic tags were not used as verified frequency counts. Offered prompt counts are not distinct concepts, candidate attempts or mark shares.
